My name is Sindhu Nelson, and I come from Anchal in Kollam district. Firstly, for making me a witness to the Marian Apparition of Our Kreupasanam Mother of Grace,
and for making me a witness for the second time, I thank our Blessed Mother. I pray to Jesus to allow me to glorify Him for the rest of my life.
When we took the Covenant here in 2019, no one had told us about Kreupasanam.
In our hometown, not many people knew about it, and I had never received a Kreupasanam newsletter. In 2019, I didn't even have WhatsApp or Youtube;
I was someone who mostly stayed confined to my home.
Apart from going wherever my husband asked me to, I was not someone who attended prayer gatherings or anything like that.
Because of that, I never even thought about using YouTube or anything similar.
No one from my family had told me about this either. At that time, when I experienced a minor physical ailment, an endoscopy was required.
During that period, I became very weak.
When I reached a point where I couldn't eat anything and was advised to get an endoscopy, I was staying at home. My husband would go out for work, and my son was studying in his twelfth grade.
So, when he went to school, he would bring food from a restaurant, as I wasn't able to cook anything.
While I was lying on the sofa, facing our prayer altar right in front of me, I was crying and fervently seeking the intercession of our Blessed Mother.
Then, I heard the word 'Kreupasanam' whisper in my ear, saying, "Come." I don't know if anyone would believe me if I say this today, but I clearly heard the word 'Kreupasanam'.
As soon as I heard that, I sat up, and the first thought that rushed to my mind was about a sister in the convent at my parish.
She was originally from Thumpoly, and she has passed away now. She had great affection for me, and after the Holy Mass on Sundays, she would give me several books.
She would bring me chocolates and books. But, as I said, since I wasn't deeply involved in prayers back then,
I would just bring those books and keep them in the cupboard. Suddenly, I remembered that the sister had handed me a folded piece of paper.
I went and opened the cupboard, and what I found was a torn Kreupasanam newsletter that the sister had given me.
When she gave it, she hadn't mentioned that it was a Kreupasanam paper. When I took it and read it, all the details about the Covenant were given at the bottom.
Then, I subscribed to the YouTube channel myself, found the Apparition prayer and the evening prayers, prayed them, and told my husband about it.
I asked him, "Take me to this place called Kreupasanam to make the Covenant, and then take me for the endoscopy."
He replied, "No, first let's go for the endoscopy, and then I will take you there." I recited this Apparition prayer for three or four days, interceding for my husband's mind to change.
After two days, he told me, "Let's go and make the Covenant." We came here, the three of us together,
and made the Covenant. Initially, I was scheduled for the endoscopy at KIMS, but after making the Covenant, my husband suggested going to Aster Medcity instead.
Then I said, "Mother, it is my decision to visit you before going." When we went to Aster, we went only after coming here and praying.
The endoscopy showed no trace of cancer or anything severe; it was cured with some minor medication.
After that, our understanding of the Covenant changed; we no longer renewed it just for our personal intentions, but to lead others to the Covenant, to help others, and to guide them forward in prayer.
Our focus entirely shifted to that, and we didn't write down any specific personal intentions. After that, I experienced more testimonies, and this is the second one.
While moving forward in the Covenant and engaging in these works of mercy, in December, I suddenly got a severe pain in my stomach.
It was a pain that made it impossible for me to bend or straighten up. I told my family, and my husband was very anxious,
wondering what kind of pain this was. We went to see a doctor, and upon scanning, they said there were signs of appendicitis.
They said that if it's appendicitis, surgery is the only option. So, as we were going to see a gastro-surgeon, before leaving, we anointed ourselves with the Covenant oil,
and prayed. When we got there, the doctor asked, "Why did you come here? There is nothing wrong in this scan," and sent us back.
But when I returned home, the pain had not subsided; it persisted just the same. My brother had passed away a year ago from liver cancer,
and my father's younger brother also died the exact same way. So, my husband took me to the same gastroenterologist who had treated my brother.
The doctor told me that since 2002, I have been getting scans, and those scans showed I had a first-grade fatty liver. Even in the scan done until this December, it showed fatty liver.
The doctor then said that since my brother died like this—his fatty liver turned into cirrhosis, and the cirrhosis developed into a tumor—it's highly likely I might also have cirrhosis.
Therefore, he asked me to undergo a FibroScan, saying that if it is indeed cirrhosis, we could start the treatment.
Because the doctor knew my brother, he had a lot of compassion for me. When I stood up, the doctor held my shoulder and said, "Don't worry,
if it is cirrhosis, I will give you a proper diet plan." When I came back home, I stood in front of the large picture of our Lord Jesus and our Mother of Kreupasanam,
that we have in our house. It is a home prepared especially for our Mother where we always gather everyone for prayer, and I said, "Oh Mother,
my brother passed away exactly like this, and some other relatives in our family also suffered the same fate.
I am not praying that I shouldn't get any illness at all, for that is not how we should love Jesus, but I know that if this particular illness strikes, following the strict diet is incredibly difficult.
Since I serve as a missionary for Kreupasanam, I visit many sick people, and I have seen patients with this condition; witnessing their pain, brings me immense sorrow.
Sometimes, I wouldn't even be able to follow that strict diet properly; if I travel anywhere, managing that diet,
would be impossible for us. I cannot handle this diet, so please, let this not be cirrhosis, do not lead me into that."
We had about eight days until the scheduled date for the FibroScan. Throughout all those days, morning and evening, I anointed myself with the Covenant oil, tracing the sign of the cross,
and continued praying exactly like this. My husband was also interceding with me; he is someone who does missionary work in 18 homes every month,
distributing the newsletters, the blessed salt, and bringing people here, immediately sharing their contact numbers with me. Before they called me for the FibroScan,
we had firmly held onto the Covenant oil and the Covenant medal. When the doctor called me for the scan,
even though there were so many people sitting there in the metro, right in front of them, I lifted my dress slightly, applied the Covenant oil on the side of my liver,
traced the sign of the cross, and placed the Covenant medal inside my clothes. I was afraid they might ask me to remove it, so I prayed,
"Blessed Mother, please don't let them ask me to take it off; it is not my liver, but yours, Mother, that should be given for this examination."
After all the tests were done and the results came half an hour later,
it showed that I didn't even have the fatty liver that I had been diagnosed with since 2002. There was no cirrhosis; my liver was completely and perfectly healthy.
Along with that, there was another testimony that Jesus and our Blessed Mother had prepared for me. Even before coming here, I had been suffering from kidney stones.
Because when my son was born, he was born with teeth, so I knew I had some underlying calcium-related issue.
Every ten months or so, I would get severe pain from the stones and end up in the casualty ward at the St. Joseph Mission Hospital in our hometown.
I would be in the casualty ward in agonizing pain, I realized that after making this Covenant, Jesus and Mother Mary had given me the grace and strength to endure that pain.
Even then, I kept my hand tightly on the Covenant medal. Still, we had to stay there overnight while they administered an IV drip, and the next day, they would ask us to see a urologist, which we would do.
But without having to take any major medications or undergo the suggested surgery, through the anointing of this Covenant oil alone, the need for surgery completely vanished.
However, for the past nine years, whenever I had this scan every ten months and saw this condition, there was a deep pain in my heart.
In January, I brought a childless couple here to meet the priest, and while they went in to see him, I was standing in front of the Adoration chapel.
As I stood there looking at them, my mind shifted to the frequent, aching pain I was experiencing on the side of my kidneys.
It was a constant, aching pain, so I prayed, "Blessed Mother, only you and Jesus know about this, perhaps I have had this since birth."
I told them, "No human in this world can remove these stones from my body, but You can do it," and then I took the oil from the lamp burning there.
I took it, made the sign of the cross on the side of my kidney, and left; and when I later did the FibroScan, the results showed that in both my kidneys,
there was not a single stone! For nine years, every ten months, scans showed 3mm and 4mm stones, and I had endured that pain simply by bearing it.
That was my second testimony, received just like that; then, on January 1st, I brought another person, a sick patient, to see the priest.
At that time, I was with our prayer group, and a young girl from our group went up to give her testimony, a testimony related to the German language.
After sharing her testimony, she came running, hugged me, and kissed me, and seeing this, about seven or eight non-Christians who had come with her,
who had also taken the Covenant, gathered around me and said we should form a group in the name of our Mother of Kreupasanam.
We created that group on January 1st with 14 members, 12 of whom are always actively praying on WhatsApp; and when we formed that group, to hold an unbroken Rosary for the first time,
I came here and met the another Sir, who gave us a blessed perpetual Rosary, blessed our group, and sent us off.
However, the day before we were to start the perpetual Rosary, I completely lost my voice; no matter how hard I tried to speak,
it was painful, and no sound would come out except a faint squeak, and even for a little sound, I had to strain as if speaking loudly into a microphone.
Because of this, I couldn't recite the perpetual Rosary; I could only sit with them, and hearing these non-Christians reciting it so loudly and with such faith,
I just sat there and cried, praying, "Blessed Mother, why am I the only one unable to pray? What happened to my voice?"
I kept asking our Mother, "Why did this happen right on the eve of doing such a good thing?"
I sat there interceding, asking Her if She couldn't restore it, but my voice didn't return; that same month, we hosted four prayer gatherings at home.
All those gatherings were at my house, and even when all 13 members prayed during those four sessions, I just sat in silence.
My husband is a busy man, and since he was extremely busy that month, he didn't ask much about my voice, which made me very sad.
He thought I lost my voice because of my existing thyroid problem, and assumed it would be fixed when we consulted a doctor later.
Every year I undergo an FNAC test, and for the last three out of four years, the FNAC results were negative; I hadn't taken it only this year.
So we went to get the FNAC done, and I anointed my neck with the Covenant oil, traced the sign of the cross,
I prayed saying, "Please give it back to me, I only need this voice to pray," and when we went to the endocrinology department for the FNAC,
the doctor knew us very well from the past three years, and noticing my face, the doctor asked if I was upset about something.
My husband replied, "Yes Doctor, Sindhu is always complaining now that she has no voice."
I then told the doctor, "It's not a complaint, my voice actually left on January 1st," and when the doctor checked, I truly had no voice, so he immediately referred me for an ENT endoscopy right there.
The endoscopy revealed two nodules causing the voice loss, which might heal on their own, but if not, both nodules would require surgery.
They also warned that even after surgery, the voice could still be lost sometimes, especially for people who strain their vocal cords by talking too much.
My husband then scolded me, saying, "You shouldn't strain your voice and pray in the group anymore; that's why you lost it. I've told you to pray softly, but you never listen."
While he was scolding me, I looked at our Mother's face and said, "Mother, if I am to pray, I cannot do it without my voice.
Praying in silence is something I can only do when sitting in an Adoration chapel.
Otherwise, when I speak to my Mother, it has to flow out straight from my heart," I prayed tearfully; the doctors prescribed tablets worth 800 rupees.
The doctor gave me the tablets and told me to take them, but when we returned home, I called the other 13 members of our group on a WhatsApp call.
I told them—we 14 are all Covenant makers who do missionary work and truly understand what the Covenant is—I told them clearly,
"I will not take this medicine; if my voice doesn't come back without it, then let it be. I only want my voice back if it is given from the altar of Kreupasanam."
So I did not take the medicine; I only anointed myself with the Covenant oil and prayed, and whenever the group members came for prayer,
they would rush to me, take the Covenant oil, trace the sign of the cross on my neck, and pray for me before leaving.
Sometimes my husband would ask me why I wasn't taking the medicine, and I replied, "No, I won't take it; let my Mother of Kreupasanam restore my voice."
He didn't argue further because he too has deep faith, and he was only asking out of concern for my voice loss; then, on February 20th,
my voice came back completely to normal without me taking a single pill, though I forgot to bring the medicine here today to show you.
I have kept the medicine unopened at home; we don't love our Mother of Kreupasanam just for personal blessings, but to bring others to the Covenant,
especially those who have fallen away from their Covenant, and my husband and I do this missionary work together.
We face a lot of mockery for the sake of our Mother of Kreupasanam, but all that ridicule feels like flowers showering down upon me.
I used to feel embarrassed initially; it has been six months since I stuck this photo of our Mother of Kreupasanam on my bag, and the insults and mockery I hear because of it,
only make my day a day of joy, even when many people mock me asking why I carry this picture of the Blessed Mother stuck on my bag.
Our reply to them is always, "We are only sorry we didn't stick it sooner," and even though this bag is worn out, I cannot bring myself to change it.
That is how much our family loves our Mother; through this, we were able to bring 20 people here, and they weren't just brought here simply, they stood firm in the Covenant.
Those 20 people in turn are bringing five more people each, and as I mentioned, we formed a group on January 1st.
It has only been two months, but united in that group, we are carrying out works of mercy, and the first major work of mercy we just did,
was for a poor family near our home, whose house was foreclosed; when they were evicted and left homeless,
they were living under a tied-up tarpaulin sheet, so we stepped in to provide them with basic facilities.
The young girl in that family suffered from a prolapsed uterus for five years, struggling without money for surgery, so all 13 of us in our group pooled together 24,000 rupees.
We collected it, gave it to them the day before yesterday, and sent her to SAT Hospital for surgery; today she has gone for her scan.
There are non-Christian families within our group doing such wonderful deeds, and their prayers are incredibly powerful; they always want to pray to our Mother of Kreupasanam.
Furthermore, regarding our missionary work, when we first took the Covenant, just like everyone else, we heard the priest say that works of mercy are essential,
and that without doing works of mercy, the Covenant remains incomplete, so we used to do works of mercy just for the sake of it,
helping a family merely for the namesake, but by the time it was between 2019 and 2025, our understanding of works of mercy evolved into visiting the sick,
taking them to the hospital, constantly visiting the homes of the patients we took, and providing them with all the help they needed,
delivering food wherever we knew people were hungry, bringing clothes to the many who had none, accompanying them to the hospital,
and for those who couldn't read, I would read everything for them and personally help them get all their medical tests done,
as time went on, our works of mercy took another turn when I realized that many who had taken the Covenant had fallen away, and were sitting in their homes,
not even knowing where their Covenant medal was, so I went to all their houses, called them, and brought them here, initially giving them a class right in their homes,
after which I brought them here, helped them renew their Covenant, and led them into doing works of mercy, as in most of the homes I visited, there were people who had renewed it three or four times,
but when asked if they had done any works of mercy, they said they had done nothing, and today, all of them are part of my group,
and they are the ones standing at the forefront of doing works of mercy now, which was the second phase of our missionary work,
the third phase of our mission was creating this group, bringing more non-Christians into it, and teaching them all the prayers I knew and had learned,
teaching the Holy Rosary to about ten people, showing them exactly how to recite it, as they didn't even know the Way of the Cross at that time,
I taught them all of that, and since I belong to the Latin Catholic rite, I took them to our churches and connected them with the reverend sisters,
for our mission, we go wherever there are people who have discontinued their Covenant, and people call me, given my number by others, telling me,
If they need to take the Covenant, I go to that house no matter how far it is, and my husband lets me go regardless of the distance.
I go there and speak with them, but I only help them take the Covenant if they give me a firm assurance that they will distribute the Marian newsletters as a missionary work,
in the early days, I used to help everyone take the Covenant, but now I only do it if they commit to distribute the newsletters,
I even pay for their travel expenses myself to bring them here, and understanding that in our hometown, some people face financial difficulties,
making it hard for them to come here every month, I build a relationship with them, visit their homes, and sit with them carrying these papers,
they have a deep desire to buy the newsletters every month and do the missionary work, but since they lack the finances to buy the paper or travel here,
my husband and I come here, pool our money together, buy the papers for all of them, and give it to them so they can go out and do the ministry,
in my own hometown, I cannot personally distribute papers anymore because I have brought so many people who are all actively doing this ministry, which allows us to travel to other places instead,
but in all our Covenant life so far, we have never distributed the newsletters at bus stands or railway stations,
nor have we done it in hospitals, because when I go to the hospital in our hometown, I see stacks of papers just left on the chairs in the OP department,
so we avoid doing that, and instead, we visit houses one by one, where I sit in each home for 10 minutes, talk about Kreupasanam, explain what the Covenant is,
and I make them listen to the important testimonies on YouTube, and as we sit there for a while, they speak from their hearts,
expressing that they always had the desire to make the Covenant but had no one to take them, so we bring them here, and this is the core of,
the missionary work we are currently doing, and for everything, I thank our Blessed Mother and Jesus, praying that the rest of my life will be solely to glorify Jesus and Mother Mary.
Psalm 27 says, “You have said, ‘Seek my face.’ My heart says to you, ‘Your face, LORD, do I seek.’ Do not hide your face from me.”
The testimony we just heard is of how this sister, Sindhu Nelson, through entering into the Marian Covenant life,
has led countless people into the protection and love of our Blessed Mother and Jesus.
Through our Baptism, each one of us is sent forth as a missionary, called and sent to love Christ,
and to proclaim Christ, which is exactly why Father Joseph always reminds us during the Covenant retreat to deepen our faith,
and to pass on this faith to those who lack it, as this is the most crucial mission of the Covenant life, and this is what we call,
missionary work; when we speak to another person about Jesus, or talk about the Apparition of our Blessed Mother,
when we share a Covenant testimony, or when we share a Covenant retreat with someone, all of these are indeed powerful acts of,
missionary work, and the newsletters of Kreupasanam is a primary tool for this mission, meant to pass on and deepen our faith,
by handing over to others these pages filled with profound divine experiences; in every month's Kreupasanam paper, we can find around a hundred high-quality, real-life testimonies,
along with an editorial that summarizes the messages given to Father Joseph by our Blessed Mother and Jesus throughout that month, which we can read,
and therefore, handing a Kreupasanam paper to another person is equivalent to passing on the Word of God and the signs of God's wonderful works.
Beloved ones, in these times, to form a new community, a community that constantly surrenders its soul to God, to form a community that lives in holiness and faithfulness in this world,
dreaming of eternity, so that in any time of global distress, in any period of poverty or lack,
we may lead a life with complete hope and faith that God is with me, and the Mighty One will do great things for me,
and the Marian Covenant is a magnificent divine plan that helps us experience the presence of God, granting us the faithful strength of belief.
Therefore, taking a Marian Covenant means that we take refuge in God, we believe in the power of God, and we declare to a world of hope,
that by the grace of God and through the intercession of our Mother's Apparition, God will grant us blessings that no one else can give, and we will truly experience them.
As she mentioned, the Holy Spirit is leading a powerful missionary work among our non-Christian brethren, and through the Covenant,
it becomes possible to bring many to the holy presence of our Blessed Mother, to pass on faith to their lives, and to provide solutions to their life's problems.
The Covenant life is a life of a faithful relationship with God, and it is a way of life that strengthens us to recognize the lacks of our brethren,
and to act as instruments of God with mercy and love, continually inspiring us to proclaim and share God,
helping us to stand firm in this world as God's missionaries, for it is a divine plan of life.
Therefore, as we move forward through the Covenant life, we become God's own, we become true brothers and sisters to humanity,
and we are able to preserve our own souls in holiness, making them fit for the journey toward eternity.
These are the living testimonies that this sister has shared at this altar, and for all the spiritual convictions and divine experiences received by this family,
let us give thanks to our Blessed Mother and her Holy Son, offering up this testimony with a round of applause.
